title: Heartbeat latency drift snapshot — weekly perf sync (May 5 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Weekly capture of an emerging tail-latency pattern correlated with periodic cluster heartbeat activity and background maintenance tasks. This note records what we observed during last week's synthetic runs, hypotheses we want to test, and concrete next steps before the Monday rollout window.

Attendees:
- Asha (owner)
- Miguel (benchmarks + infra)
- Jin (runtime)
- Sofia (observability)
- Theo (SRE)

High-level summary:
- Starting Apr 28 we've seen recurring p99 spikes (~250–350ms above baseline) that align with a ~5m cadence across a subset of canary nodes. p50/p95 mostly stable, but tail gets worse after ~10–15k requests into a long mixed-seq run.
- Reproduced in controlled synthetic mixed-sequence workload (mix described below) on canary cluster c4. Not observed in small-batch constant-seq tests.
- Quick triage suggests interaction between: (a) heartbeat-driven light GC/cleanup process, (b) KV cache eviction windows, and (c) continuous-batching heuristics that open new batches when a warmup pause occurs.

Repro setup (what we ran)
- Cluster: canary-c4 (8xA100 equivalent), isolated from production routing.
- Model: rwd-7b-q (float16 serving variant), kv-cache enabled.
- Workload: mixed sequence lengths: 60% short (16–32 tokens), 30% medium (64–128 tokens), 10% long (512 tokens). Arrival: Poisson lambda tuned to target 400 qps baseline.
- Duration: 90 min runs, repeated 6 times across two nodes.
- Instrumentation: full tracing enabled, batch size histogram, KV cache hit ratio, kernel selection logging at info.

Observed signals (key artifacts)
- Latency: baseline p50=12ms, p95=38ms, average p99 during spikes=430ms (typical p99 baseline=90–120ms). Spikes lasted ~6–14s and recurred with ~5m periodicity on node-1 and node-3.
- Batching: bursts where a single large batch opened (batch size temporarily jumped 3–5x) coincident with the spike start timestamp.
- KV cache: short-term drop in local KV hit ratio from ~97% to ~60% during spike windows; concurrent remote KV fetches observed.
- Heartbeat/maintenance: system heartbeat log showed background 'cardinality-trim' runs that execute every 5m and do small memory compaction + metadata scrubs on the same nodes.
- Kernels: a handful of kernel falls-back to a slower path (kernel_fallback_count increases) during spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Heartbeat maintenance triggers a brief memory compaction which evicts or invalidates local level-0 KV caches; first few requests after compaction miss and cause remote KV fetch + batch-opening jitter => tail spike. (Most likely)
2) Continuous-batching heuristic interprets the inter-request gap after compaction as an opportunity to open a large batch; that batch triggers kernel selection path that is inefficient for the current sequence mix.
3) Scheduler/OOM protective preemption occasionally delays workers while compaction runs, causing backpressure accumulating into a single large scheduling reschedule and temporary stall.
4) Environment anomaly: a monitoring job (prometheus scrape) increases I/O at same time, combining with compaction to produce a compound effect.

Test runs and results (what we validated quickly)
- KV-affinity pinning test: forced KV cache to be pinned (no eviction) during a short run -> spikes disappeared in 3/3 repeats. p99 returned to baseline.
- Disable heartbeat maintenance (on canary) -> spikes disappeared. Negative test suggests heartbeats are causal.
- Adjust continuous-batching hold-time from 8ms -> 20ms -> reduces large-batch openings but increases p50 slightly. Results: p95 improved (fewer spikes) but throughput dropped ~4%.
- Simulated spike w/forced remote KV fetches on workload with constant small seq -> did not reproduce the magnitude of spike, which suggests mixed-seq interaction.

Open data / logs to review (links)
- tracing spans: dashboard:perf/heartbeat-drift-05-2026 (linked above)
- node logs: s3://redwood-canaries/heartbeat-drift/may05/node-1.log (TODO: permission)
- kcache metrics: PromQL queries attached in INF-2384

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Jin: add KV eviction trace tagging (annotate spans when compaction runs) so we can correlate trace<->cache state. Deadline: 2026-05-10.
- Miguel: run 3x A/B runs on canary-c4 with (a) heartbeat off, (b) pinned kv, (c) raised batching hold-time. Collect full traces and batch histograms. Deadline: 2026-05-08.
- Theo: evaluate background maintenance schedule (can we jitter heartbeats across nodes?) and propose a soft-stagger patch. Deadline: 2026-05-12.
- Sofia: add alert rule to detect p99 relative jump >200ms within a 10s window for canary clusters. Also surface KV local-hit drops in the perf dashboard. Deadline: 2026-05-11.
- Asha: prepare short rollback plan for Monday rollout (if similar pattern surfaces in canaries) and draft a customer-facing note template in case of impact. Deadline: 2026-05-09.

Decisions captured:
- Blocker? Not blocking rollout yet, but we will hold full rollout to additional canaries until Miguel completes A/B runs and Jin ships the eviction trace tagging.
- Short-term mitigation: pin KV on critical nodes + stagger heartbeats, and increase batching hold-time by 2x for canary cluster only.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Does pinning KV cause memory pressure on longer running workloads (we saw one OOM alarm once in stress test)? Need to validate with longer 6h soak.
- Are there model-variant-specific kernel fallbacks? Need to cross-check kernel selection rollback with other models (rwd-13b, rwd-3b).
- Does the same pattern occur for dedicated customer pools where heartbeats and maintenance may be configured differently?

Notes to self / quick wins:
- Quick experiment: stagger heartbeats by random(0,30s) across nodes and run 2x quick tests — cheap and non-invasive.
- Consider a lightweight 'prefetch' path: on first miss after compaction, do a micro-prefetch for expected KV keys for the next 10 requests to smooth the very first fetch penalty.

Next sync:
- Short follow-up standup Wed 2026-05-07 11:30 PT to check Miguel's first A/B run artifacts. Full perf sync Mon 2026-05-11 9:00 PT to decide rollout.

Appendix: quick numeric table (single run sample)
- baseline throughput: 400 qps
- run length: 90 min
- normal p99: 95ms
- observed p99 during spikes: 430ms (avg of spike windows)
- KV local hit ratio outside spikes: 97%
- KV local hit ratio during spikes: 60%

If you have additional traces or want to run a local reproduction, ping me in #serving-runtime-bench and drop the trace id.
